objective: Reproduce the reported symptom, trace root cause, classify severity, confirm the plan's size still holds
summary: A reproduction test ran at backend HEAD 8fda17fa (equal to its merge-base) and 3 cases passed against today's behaviour: reset accepts a 6-character password past validation and fails only at token lookup, change-password returns 200 for an 8-character password with no symbol, and sign-up does not refuse a 12-character password that has no uppercase letter. The root cause is that each request struct carries only a length attribute (12, 6, 8) and no endpoint checks letter, digit or symbol classes; the only server rule set lives in the browser. Exactly three hash_password call sites set a customer password (signup and reset in auth.rs, change in users.rs); admin create-user, test-account provisioning, backup codes and email OTP are out of scope. All three frontend consumers already show the server's error message. No intended, as-built or design doc states a password rule, so there is no intent conflict and no open product question. Severity security, size L and full track still hold; risk area authorization (credential-setting guard).
requirements: 917 AC1: A customer resetting a password needs at least 12 characters, the same as at sign-up.
917 AC2: A signed-in customer changing their password needs at least 12 characters.
917 AC3: The page and the server give the same message about the minimum.
917 AC4: Existing shorter passwords keep working until their owner changes them.
964 AC1: On staging, sign-up, reset and change password each refuse a password that misses any of the five rules, and say which rule is missing.
964 AC2: A password that meets all five rules is accepted on all three.
964 AC3: Customers whose existing password breaks the new rules can still sign in.
